svg.title: Proof. Antisymmetry of Q gives (RJ1) for ρQ. Differentiating (RJ4), subtracting the reversed derivative and using (RJ3), ∂ial −∂lai = [2Qil + P k xk∂kQil]/(j + 2) = Qil by Euler’s identity in degree j. For (2), P k xk(∂ka′ i −∂ia′ k) = (j + 1)a′ i −∂i(P k xka′ k) + a′ i, again by Euler’s identity, which is (j + 2)(a′ i −∂iλ). If a′ is radial then λ = 0, which is the second half of (1). (3) follows: two potentials with the same curl have the same image under ρ curl, so they differ by a gradient, and a radial gradient ∂μ has x · ∂μ = (j + 2)μ = 0. Equality of homogeneous diagonal polynomials is equality of symmetric tensors by polarization.
